title: For 3D assets, does using a pipeline of tools actually work?
author: SingleTarget6924
selftext: I'm working on a passion project right now and I've noticed people using workflows such as using Claude to drive softwares or starting with AI tools and cleaning them up in blender. does it actually improve the outcome or efficiency? I thought it would occupy the already limited token availability. Or would a one-stop software based on blender work better?

comments.author: MichaelEmouse
comments.body:
You can use Claude with the Blender MCP add-on to have Claude make game assets. Iirc, Claude Code can directly control Blender or just about anything you want.

  
It's ridiculously more time efficient than doing yourself. Whether the outcome is better depends on what you could make yourself but it's certainly better than what I could make.

replies.author: Suecotero
replies.body: Yeah but how do you make Claude/Blender make assets that don't look like they were made in 1995?

replies.author: Soul_Mate_4ever
replies.body: Say Claude. Make assets that don’t look like they were made in 1995.

replies.author: ffktiv
replies.body: You create two agents, one for modelling and one for validating the results and have them go like 5 or 10 rounds of that. In opencode you switch to asset lead and tell the agent to write up a markdown doc about what to do. I got some decent results as a test but didn't want to burn my credits on just that so I never finished mine. After 5 rounds, my vehicle looked pretty decent. Someone called this method a gauntlet loop.

replies.author: MichaelEmouse
replies.body:
Is that in ultracode since you're using two agents? 

I'm new to Claude Code and have never used two agents together.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Yes but Claude eats up tokens like crazy for 3D asset creation. For simple assets, it's simply better to use a image to 3D model because they're much cheaper.

replies.author: PupperRobot
replies.body: Tripo smart mesh in unbeatable currently until something betters comes up. You can use both meshy and tripo and have Claude reduce the vertex count too. But tripo's smart mesh and smart uv are great right now.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body:
Yes it does, i use like 15+ software in my creative workflow and i dont mean generative AI tools. 3ds Max, Maya, Zbrush, Substance 3D Painter, Substance 3D Designer, Substance 3D Sampler,  Marvelous Designer, Unreal Engine, Marmoset Toolbag, Gaea, Speedtree, Photoshop, sometimes Illustrator and other Adobe CC software and all of that before even counting RizomUV which is for UV unwrapping and add-ons i use for a bunch of these software (Animbot, mGear, Ornatrix and some other). 

There is a risk of having such a massive pipeline and in my case its also very expensive too, but im a professional and i learned how to deal with that and i can say it saves me hundreds, possibly even thousands of hours per year compared to a workflow where i only would use Blender as main DCC with some additional packages supporting it like Substance Painter.

comments.author: HaMMeReD
comments.body:
I have a project that takes pictures of a dog or cat (could be a human too, but I do pets).

That uses Gen AI to convert to a contact-sheet, 4-up (top/back/front/side) in a pose

Then I use Meshy to generate a mesh

Then I use Meshy again to texture it

Then I use a custom pass to prepare for 3D printing

Then I print.

Happy with the assets I got so far, but generally some are bad, you might need to retry on any stage.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body:
Workflows and pipelines is the way to go. Amateurs ask Claude to make something. That wastes a lot of tokens. Instead, tell Claude to make a tool, then use the tool. Use connections into blender etc.

I made a tool that can take screenshots in Unity. Without the editor. The tool runs inside of a headless Unity. So now I can tell it: go make lots of screenshots for my Steam page. And it barely costs any tokens cause it runs inside Unity and not in Claude.
